title: Action de Galois sur Teichmüller : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (continuing from p.84): X is a K-variety (K a number field), Γ = Gal(K̄/K), and I ⊂ X(K) is a set of K-rational base points containing x0. Γ acts on the profinite fundamental groupoid Π̂_1(X_K̄; I) on base points I. The previous page noted that this action is determined by two things: the action on the vertex group π̂_1(X, x0), and the action on the π̂_1(X,x0)-torsors of étale paths from x0 to each x_i, labelled (41).

This page makes that into explicit data.
(42) For each i ∈ I, choose a 'discrete' path l_i from x0 to x_i. This means a topological path in X(ℂ), or an element of the discrete groupoid Π_1, sitting densely inside the profinite path torsor (41). For each u ∈ Γ, record the element f_{l_i}^{(u)} ∈ π̂_1(X,x0) measuring the defect u(l_i) versus l_i (e.g. u(l_i) = l_i · f_{l_i}^{(u)}, up to convention). The map u ↦ f_{l_i}^{(u)} is a non-abelian 1-cocycle.
(43) Choose generators λ_j (j ∈ J) of the discrete group π_1(X,x0). Record the elements f_{λ_j}^{(u)} or g_{λ_j}^{(u)} that express u(λ_j). For P^1 − {0,1,∞} this is the familiar form u(λ) = f^{-1} λ^{χ(u)} f, as in Ihara-style or later Drinfeld–Ihara-style descriptions.

By density of the discrete groupoid in its profinite completion, (42)+(43) determine the whole Γ-action on Π̂_1(X; I). A marginal addition says this holds 'en principe', referring back to p.8x.

Grothendieck then criticises this description. It is concise, but it depends on arbitrary choices: the base point x0, the paths l_i, and the generators. He finds this artificial and, in the long run, impracticable. This is especially so when a symmetry group G of K-automorphisms acts and I is G-stable, since (next page) one almost never finds a G-fixed point x0.

This motivates the next pages. They give a 'symmetric' calculation principle using groupoids on G-stable sets of base points. They also reduce the Galois action on π_1(X; I) to π_1(U_{0,3}): Lefschetz-type theorems plus Belyi's theorem should give a curve I ⊂ C → X that is π_1-surjective, together with a map C → U_{0,3}.
errors: No mathematical error. Minor implicit point: the Γ-action on π̂_1(X_K̄, x0) and on the path torsors needs the base points to be K-rational (or tangential/Γ-stable as a set with a twisted action); this is assumed via I ⊂ X(K).
'Determined by' should be read via continuity/density of the discrete paths and generators in the profinite completions; this is presumably the 'en principe' of the margin.

ideas.what: Describe the Galois action on a profinite fundamental groupoid with several rational base points by cocycles on chosen discrete paths x0→x_i plus the action on generators of π_1(X,x0)
ideas.modern_name: Galois action on étale path torsors; non-abelian cocycles f_σ (Ihara/Drinfeld–Ihara parametrisation)
ideas.where_published: Spirit present in Esquisse d'un programme §2, not this explicit formula

ideas.what: Critique of base-point/generator choices as artificial; need for a choice-free 'symmetric' description when a symmetry group G acts and I is G-stable with no G-fixed point
ideas.modern_name: Fundamental groupoid with G-stable set of base points (base-point philosophy)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Esquisse d'un programme, 1984); Deligne 1989 for tangential base points

ideas.what: (next page) Reduce Galois action on π_1(X;I) of any smooth quasi-projective X/K to π_1(U_{0,3}) via a Lefschetz curve C ⊃ I and a Belyi map C→U_{0,3}
ideas.modern_name: Belyi + Lefschetz reduction; faithfulness of Γ_Q on π_1 of varieties

deep.surprise_reason: This is an early, explicit working-out of the groupoid-with-many-base-points viewpoint, motivated by symmetries without fixed points. That viewpoint is well known from Esquisse d'un programme and was later systematised by Deligne and Ihara. The page is a nice archival witness of its genesis but contains nothing absent from the literature.
transcription_corrections: Line 2: 'l_i est un chemin dans Π_1(X, x_i)' — the reading is uncertain; the sense is a path in the (discrete) groupoid from x0 to x_i, e.g. Π_1(X; x0, x_i).
The marginal insertion reads roughly 'qui est[?] ... en principe, comme dit p. 8[1?]' and is attached to 'suffisent'.
'a le désavantage néanmoins de reposer' → the text struck 'de reposer' and continued 'de se référer à des choix arbitraires'.
'le choix d'un {+point-base+} [-origine-] x0' — the superscript replacement is likely 'point base' rather than 'base'.
Last line: 'opérant[?] à partir[?] I stable par G' → probably 'opérant, et avec I stable par G'.
